text:
alex: quick q about sideplane vs central CP: if we run a local control agent in customer VPC, how should callbacks/egress preserve source IPs for customer allowlists?
nisha: two broad approaches: 1) preserve src by routing through customer-facing ENI (no SNAT) or 2) SNAT at our regional relay and present a stable egress IP. each has ops/cost/prod tradeoffs.
linus: preserving src is best for strict allowlists but adds complexity: peering/route propagation, ENI lifecycle, failover semantics across AZ/region. tends to be brittle unless dedicated.
alex: right. my naive proposal: default = regional SNAT (simpler). sideplane can opt into a src-preserve mode that pins an ENI/EIP (reserved) per-tenant. for customers that need pure IP allowlist we charge/gate it.
olivia: pinning per-tenant means reserved ENIs or NAT gateways — will increase our per-customer infra cost and billing complexity. is there a middle ground?
nisha: we could offer an aggregated static-IP pool per region shared across tenants and map requests with an X-Redwood-Tenant header for app-level identification. that helps many use-cases but not network-level allowlists.
linus: exactly. header mapping doesn't solve IP-based allowlists. so constraint: network allowlist customers must be Enterprise/dedicated. we should document that.
alex: hybrid idea: prefer src-preserve when the sideplane has an ENI available; otherwise fallback to shared static pool + tenant header. require observable fallback metric.
infra-bot: perf-estimate: sideplane per-tenant NAT ~+0.7ms p50 on request path. cost-estimate: depends on EIP count & NAT hours. creating cost ticket.
olivia: rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag sideplane egress modes. beta with 5 pilot customers. default behavior stays regional SNAT. provide a migration runbook and templates for customer allowlist onboarding.
linus: operational concern: route withdraw/failover blackholes. if sideplane withdraws prefix during outage traffic will shift to regional relay and src-preserve will be lost. we need soft-handoff and health checks.
alex: agree. propose withdraw grace-window (30s) + active health-probed switch. full tests in spike.
nisha: also add tenant-level config field egress_mode: ["regional-snat","shared-static","src-preserve"]. surfaces in UI and audit logs.
olivia: test matrix: allowlist acceptance test, failover SLO test (simulate peering loss), metrics: fallback_count, pinnedENI_count, sharedPool_utilization. docs + pricing draft before beta.
alex: action items: linus -> spike BGP/route-prop options (3d), infra -> EIP/NAT cost projection + INFRA ticket, olivia -> rollout + docs (7d). i'll open RFC-followup thread with diagrams.
linus: ack. i'll include failure diagrams and sequence diagrams for withdraw/soft-handoff.
infra-bot: ticket INFRA-5234 created: "sideplane egress modes cost + failover spike"
alex: thanks all, will loop in sales for pricing constraints and solutions for enterprise allowlist customers.
